title: Landing page
purpose: The first page anyone sees. It explains the service in one line and lets visitors check a price before creating an account.
example: Prices come from the real price list (base fare + per-km rate). Rental cards come from vehicles owners have offered.

callouts.title: Headline
callouts.text: Says exactly what ZamMove does and where: van and truck booking in Zamboanga City.

callouts.title: Quick price checker
callouts.text: Tabs to get a hauling estimate, check a rental price, or track a trip with a booking reference.

callouts.title: Instant estimate
callouts.text: Visitors pick two places and see the fare right away, no sign-up needed.

callouts.title: Vehicle types and prices
callouts.text: From 3-wheelers to 6-wheeler trucks, each with capacity and price.

callouts.title: Self-drive rental
callouts.text: Rental models offered by verified owners, with the lowest daily rate.

title: Create an account (empty form)
purpose: New customers register with their personal details. Everyone starts as a customer; driver and vehicle-owner roles are applied for later from the account page.
example: All fields are required. The customer must be 18 or older and accept the Terms and Privacy Policy.

callouts.title: Full name and birthday
callouts.text: Used on receipts and to check the customer is 18 or older.

callouts.title: Mobile number
callouts.text: Philippine number (09…). The verification code is sent here.

callouts.title: Email
callouts.text: Used to log in and for booking updates.

callouts.title: Password
callouts.text: At least 8 characters with a letter and a number; stored encrypted.

callouts.title: Terms and privacy
callouts.text: Must be accepted before an account is created.

title: Create an account (filled in)
purpose: The same form completed. Password rules are checked as the customer types, and both passwords must match.
example: Mika Torres, born 1995, 0917 123 4510, Sta. Catalina, mika@zammove.ph.

callouts.title: Confirm password
callouts.text: Must match; mistakes are caught before sending.

callouts.title: Create account
callouts.text: Creates the account and logs the customer in. The account starts as “not verified”.

title: Verify the account (6-digit code)
purpose: Right after sign-up the customer must enter a 6-digit code sent to their phone and email. This proves the number and email are real before anyone can book a truck.
example: SMS is not connected in this prototype, so the code is shown on screen. In production it arrives by SMS.

callouts.title: Verification banner
callouts.text: Stays on Home until the account is verified.

callouts.title: Where the code comes from
callouts.text: In the real service this is the SMS / email message.

callouts.title: Code box
callouts.text: The customer types the 6 digits here.

title: Before verification: booking is blocked
purpose: If the customer tries to book before verifying, the server refuses and explains why. Rentals are blocked the same way.
example: Mika filled in a move from Sta. Catalina to Tumaga, but has not entered her code yet.

callouts.title: Clear message
callouts.text: “Verify your account first”: nothing is booked and no driver is notified.

title: Entering the verification code
purpose: The customer types the code and taps Verify. Wrong codes are rejected.

callouts.title: Verify
callouts.text: Checks the code on the server.

title: After verification: ready to book
purpose: The banner disappears and booking and renting are unlocked. This is the customer home from now on.
example: Mika Torres, verified.

callouts.title: Unlocked
callouts.text: No more verification banner; every action is available.

title: Log in
purpose: Returning users log in. One account can hold several roles (customer, driver, vehicle owner); the workspace switcher moves between them.
example: The same login page is used by customers, drivers, owners, cashiers and administrators.

title: Wrong password
purpose: A wrong password shows how many tries are left, without saying whether the email exists.
example: “Invalid email or password. 4 attempts left.”

title: Locked after 5 wrong tries
purpose: After 5 wrong passwords the account is locked for 60 seconds.
example: “Too many failed attempts. Login is locked for 60 seconds.”

callouts.title: Temporary lock
callouts.text: Slows down anyone trying to guess a password.

title: Forgot password: step 1
purpose: To reset a password the user enters their email and date of birth. A one-time code is then sent to them.
example: ana@zammove.ph, born 1990-01-01.

callouts.title: Date of birth
callouts.text: A second check that this is the owner of the account.

title: Forgot password: step 2 (code and new password)
purpose: The user enters the code they received and chooses a new password. Old login sessions stop working.
example: Code 607616 (shown on screen in this prototype; sent by SMS/email in production).

callouts.title: Reset code
callouts.text: Expires after a short time; wrong codes are refused.

callouts.title: Update password
callouts.text: Then log in with the new password.

title: Book a haul (truck with driver)
purpose: The customer enters pickup, drop-off, vehicle, date and items. The fare is computed instantly; the request then goes to available drivers.
example: Sta. Catalina → Tumaga, L300 Van, tomorrow 9:00, 1 extra mover, discount code WELCOME (5% off).

callouts.title: Pickup and drop-off
callouts.text: Search a barangay or landmark, tap the map, or use the phone’s location. Zamboanga City only.

callouts.title: Vehicle type
callouts.text: Capacity and base fare for each type. Only types with a free vehicle at that time can be booked.

callouts.title: Schedule
callouts.text: The system checks a vehicle is free for the whole trip window.

callouts.title: Items and instructions
callouts.text: What to carry and notes for the driver; this becomes the cargo checklist at pickup.

callouts.title: Fare estimate
callouts.text: Base + distance + movers + 5% service fee − discount. Paid 50% at pickup and 50% after delivery.

callouts.title: Submit
callouts.text: Sends the request to eligible drivers.

title: Step 1 · Customer: waiting for a driver (before)
purpose: The booking is sent. Until a driver accepts, the customer sees “Pending” and can cancel for free.
example: BK-5DI0VV: Sta. Catalina → Tumaga, L300 Van, tomorrow 9:00.

callouts.title: Status: Pending
callouts.text: Waiting for the first eligible driver to accept.

callouts.title: Free cancellation
callouts.text: No fee while Pending; 10% after a driver accepts.

callouts.title: Cancel
callouts.text: The customer can still cancel at no charge.

title: Step 2 · Driver: new booking request
purpose: Every eligible driver sees the request. The system shows why this driver may take it; the first to accept gets the job.
example: Leo Garcia (white L300, ZAM 3388) is Available and free tomorrow morning.

callouts.title: Customer privacy
callouts.text: The customer’s name and phone are shared only after the driver accepts.

callouts.title: Job details
callouts.text: Route, schedule, cargo, movers and price. Eligibility (approved vehicle, right type, free schedule) is checked on the server.

callouts.title: Accept
callouts.text: Assigns the booking to this driver and notifies the customer.

callouts.title: Decline
callouts.text: Hides it for this driver only.

title: Step 3 · Customer: driver assigned (after)
purpose: As soon as a driver accepts, the customer sees who is coming: photo, name, rating, vehicle, plate and color.
example: Leo Garcia · white Mitsubishi L300 · plate ZAM 3388.

callouts.title: Status: Accepted
callouts.text: The driver is committed to this schedule.

callouts.title: Driver and vehicle card
callouts.text: So the customer can recognise the truck at pickup.

callouts.title: View profile
callouts.text: Full profile with reviews and the vehicle photo.

title: Step 4 · Driver: start heading to the pickup
purpose: On the trip day the driver opens the Active trip page and taps “Heading to pickup”. Each tap moves the trip one step forward.
example: BK-5DI0VV for Mika Torres, tomorrow 9:00.

callouts.title: Navigate
callouts.text: Opens Waze with the pickup address.

callouts.title: Next step button
callouts.text: Only the next allowed status is offered.

title: Step 5 · Customer: driver on the way (live map)
purpose: The customer follows the truck on a live map and sees the estimated minutes to the pickup. A Waze link is a backup.
example: Leo Garcia is near Sta. Maria, heading to Sta. Catalina.

callouts.title: Live map
callouts.text: Pickup, drop-off, driver position and route so far.

callouts.title: Live status
callouts.text: Last update, GPS accuracy, distance and minutes to the pickup.

title: Step 6 · Driver: on the way, sharing location
purpose: While driving, the phone shares its location for the customer’s map. On arrival the driver taps “I’ve arrived at pickup”.
example: Live location: Sharing. Waze link: Shared.

callouts.title: Live location
callouts.text: Sent about every 10 seconds, only during the trip, only to this customer and staff.

callouts.title: Arrived at pickup
callouts.text: Moves the trip to “Awaiting Down Payment”.

title: Step 7 · Customer: pay the 50% down payment
purpose: Before loading, the customer pays half. They can pay the driver in cash, or send GCash and enter the reference number here.
example: Down payment ₱1,240.00 by GCash, ref 7012398765432 (GCash is simulated in this prototype).

callouts.title: Status
callouts.text: Loading cannot start until the down payment is recorded.

callouts.title: GCash amount and reference
callouts.text: The reference is checked: 10–13 digits and never used before.

callouts.title: Submit GCash proof
callouts.text: The driver confirms it arrived before it counts.

title: Step 8 · Driver: confirm the down payment
purpose: The driver sees the customer’s GCash reference pre-filled, checks it arrived, adds any cash, and records the payment. GCash + cash must equal exactly 50%.
example: GCash 7012398765432 pre-filled with the full down payment.

callouts.title: Customer’s proof
callouts.text: Shown so the driver can check the GCash app.

callouts.title: Amounts
callouts.text: GCash, cash and reference; they must add up to the amount due.

callouts.title: Record payment
callouts.text: Moves the trip to “Down Payment Confirmed”.

title: Step 9 · Customer: down payment confirmed
purpose: The payment shows as recorded by the driver, and the trip moves on to loading. Every payment appears in the customer’s payment history.
example: Down: paid in full · Final: due after delivery.

callouts.title: Status
callouts.text: Half is paid; loading can start.

callouts.title: Payment record
callouts.text: Method, reference, amount and who confirmed it.

title: Step 10 · Driver: load and describe the cargo
purpose: After loading, the driver describes what was loaded and taps “Items loaded”. This note is part of the trip record.
example: Sofa (wrapped), 4 boxes, refrigerator upright and strapped.

callouts.title: Cargo description
callouts.text: Required; what was loaded and in what condition.

title: Step 11 · Customer: Start PIN (pre-departure)
purpose: The truck cannot leave without the customer’s one-time Start PIN. The customer shows it (or the QR) to the driver at the pickup — it proves the right driver is with the right customer.
example: Start PIN 177160. Valid 30 minutes; locks after 5 wrong tries.

callouts.title: Start PIN
callouts.text: Only on the customer’s phone; never sent to the driver.

callouts.title: Pre-departure verification
callouts.text: PIN, plate, cargo checklist and both confirmations.

callouts.title: New PIN
callouts.text: Generate a new one if it expires.

title: Step 12 · Driver: enter the Start PIN
purpose: The driver types the PIN the customer shows (or scans the QR). A wrong PIN counts as an attempt.
example: PIN 177160 entered.

title: Step 13 · Driver: PIN verified, check the plate
purpose: With the PIN verified, the driver confirms the plate of the vehicle being used. It must match the vehicle assigned to the booking.
example: Plate ZAM 3388 (white L300).

callouts.title: PIN verified
callouts.text: Time-stamped; the PIN can’t be reused.

callouts.title: Plate check
callouts.text: Prevents using a different, unapproved vehicle.

title: Step 14 · Driver: cargo checklist and confirmation
purpose: The driver ticks every booked item, enters the piece count, confirms fragile items are padded and strapped, and confirms. A count that differs from the booking is reported automatically.
example: 6 pieces · every item ticked · fridge padded and strapped.

callouts.title: Item checklist
callouts.text: Every booked item must be ticked.

callouts.title: Progress
callouts.text: The steps at the top turn complete one by one; next the customer confirms.

title: Step 15 · Customer: review and confirm the cargo
purpose: The customer sees the driver’s checklist and confirms it matches what was loaded — or reports a missing, extra or damaged item before departure.
example: Sofa, 4 boxes, refrigerator: all ticked.

callouts.title: Report a problem
callouts.text: Opens a discrepancy staff must resolve.

title: Step 16 · Driver: authorize departure
purpose: Only when the PIN, plate, checklist and both confirmations are complete can the driver authorize departure.
example: All five checks complete.

callouts.title: Authorize departure
callouts.text: Moves the trip to “In Transit”. Without it, the truck may not leave.

title: Step 17 · Customer: in transit
purpose: The items are on the way. The live map now shows the minutes to the drop-off.
example: Leo Garcia between Sta. Catalina and Tumaga.

title: Step 18 · Driver: in transit
purpose: On arrival the driver taps “Arrived at destination”.
example: Heading to Tumaga.

callouts.title: Arrived at destination
callouts.text: Next the customer’s Delivery PIN is needed.

title: Step 19 · Customer: Delivery PIN
purpose: At the drop-off the customer checks the items first, then gives the driver the Delivery PIN. Giving the PIN means “I received everything in good condition”.
example: Delivery PIN 242596.

callouts.title: Delivery PIN
callouts.text: Proof of delivery; only on the customer’s phone.

callouts.title: Report instead
callouts.text: If something is missing or damaged, report it instead of giving the PIN.

title: Step 20 · Driver: confirm delivery with the PIN
purpose: The driver enters the customer’s Delivery PIN and the delivery condition. An optional photo can be attached. This is the proof of delivery.
example: PIN 242596 · “All 6 pieces delivered to the 3rd floor, no damage.”

callouts.title: Delivery PIN
callouts.text: Wrong PINs count as attempts and lock after 5.

callouts.title: Delivery record
callouts.text: Condition note, optional photo; saved with the time.

title: Step 21 · Customer: delivered, final payment due
purpose: Delivery is confirmed and the remaining 50% is now due. The customer can pay the driver in cash or send GCash.
example: Status: Awaiting Final Payment.

title: Step 22 · Driver: collect the final payment
purpose: The driver records the final 50%. Once recorded the trip is completed.

callouts.title: Cash amount
callouts.text: GCash + cash must equal the amount due.

title: Step 23 · Customer: completed, rate the driver
purpose: The move is complete and fully paid. The customer sees the proof of delivery and rates the driver.
example: 5 stars: “Very careful with the fridge and on time.”

callouts.title: Completed
callouts.text: Both halves paid; delivery confirmed by PIN.

callouts.title: Rate the driver
callouts.text: 1–5 stars; ratings appear on the driver’s profile.

callouts.title: Comment
callouts.text: Shown to future customers without the reviewer’s name.

title: Step 24 · Customer: review saved (after)
purpose: The finished booking stays in the Past tab with its full history, payments, receipt and review.
example: BK-5DI0VV · Completed · ★★★★★.

callouts.title: Review
callouts.text: Saved and added to the driver’s rating.

callouts.title: Past bookings
callouts.text: Every finished move with its records.

title: Step 25 · Driver: earnings and weekly remittance
purpose: The completed trip is added to the driver’s earnings. Each week the driver remits the company share (80%) and keeps 20%; a cashier verifies it.
example: BK-5DI0VV collected in full.

callouts.title: Weekly remittance
callouts.text: Once a week by GCash reference or cash; a cashier verifies it.

title: Rental step 1 · Renter: choose dates and a model
purpose: Self-drive rental. The renter picks the dates first; each model then shows how many units are free on every one of those days.
example: Carla needs a van for 2 days. Mitsubishi L300 shows “2 of 2 available”.

callouts.title: Rental dates
callouts.text: Units booked on any of those days count as unavailable.

callouts.title: Model card
callouts.text: Photo, type, seats and daily rate.

callouts.title: Availability
callouts.text: Free units for the chosen dates.

callouts.title: My rentals
callouts.text: The renter’s rentals and their status.

title: Rental step 2 · Renter: model information and units
purpose: General information about the model, then every unit free on the chosen dates. Each unit shows its own rate and refundable deposit, set by its owner.
example: L300: 1.5 tons · 10 ft, 3 seats, manual, diesel. Blue 2020 at ₱2,200/day (₱6,000 deposit); Pearl White 2023 at ₱2,500/day (₱8,000 deposit).

callouts.title: Model and best use
callouts.text: What the vehicle is good for.

callouts.title: General information
callouts.text: Capacity, seats, transmission, fuel, years, rate and deposit range.

callouts.title: Available unit
callouts.text: Color, year, part of the plate, owner, deposit and total.

title: Rental step 3 · Renter: request form
purpose: The renter sees the full amount to pay before pickup, gives the pickup and return places and uploads ID and license photos. The rules of the rental are listed before submitting.
example: Pearl White L300 · 2 days · ₱5,000 rental + ₱8,000 refundable deposit = ₱13,000 before pickup.

callouts.title: Price summary
callouts.text: Rate × days + this vehicle’s deposit = total to pay before pickup.

callouts.title: License check
callouts.text: Must be valid until the return date.

callouts.title: ID and license photos
callouts.text: The owner compares them at pickup.

callouts.title: Before you rent
callouts.text: Contract, full payment, 6 handover photos, location sharing, deposit claims.

callouts.title: Submit
callouts.text: The dates are held while the request is pending.

title: Rental step 4 · Owner: offer vehicles (rate and deposit)
purpose: Owners choose which approved vehicles to rent out and set, per vehicle, the daily rate, the refundable deposit (at least ₱5,000) and the details renters see.
example: Olga’s Pearl White L300: ₱2,500/day and an ₱8,000 deposit. The hauling L300s are not offered.

callouts.title: Deposit per vehicle
callouts.text: From ₱5,000; a more valuable vehicle can ask more.

callouts.title: Not offered
callouts.text: Hauling-only vehicles stay off the Rent page.

callouts.title: Save or stop
callouts.text: Any time; existing rentals keep their deposit.

title: Rental step 5 · Owner: approve the request
purpose: The owner sees the renter, phone, dates, price, license and the ID photos, then approves (dates re-checked) or rejects with a reason. Approving issues the rental contract.
example: Carla Mendoza requested ZAM 5150 for 2 days.

callouts.title: Request details
callouts.text: Renter, phone, dates, price, deposit, license.

callouts.title: Approve
callouts.text: Re-checks the dates and issues the contract.

title: Rental step 6 · Renter: approved, contract waiting
purpose: After approval the renter sees the full plate and the owner’s contact, the rental contract waiting for signatures, and the full amount to pay before pickup.
example: Contract CT-… is issued. Carla must sign it and pay ₱13,000 before pickup.

callouts.title: Print
callouts.text: For signing on paper at pickup.

callouts.title: Payment
callouts.text: GCash or cash; the full amount before pickup.

callouts.title: Cancel
callouts.text: Possible until the vehicle is released.

title: Rental step 7 · The rental contract (digital copy)
purpose: The same contract the owner prints. It freezes the parties, vehicle, dates and money at approval, lists 14 clauses, has a handover record and signature boxes, and ends with a fingerprint code that proves nothing was changed.
example: Olga Navarro (owner) and Carla Mendoza (renter), Pearl White L300 ZAM 5150, ₱5,000 + ₱8,000 deposit.

callouts.title: Parties
callouts.text: Names, phones, addresses and the renter’s license.

callouts.title: Terms and conditions
callouts.text: Use, location sharing, photos, damage, deposit claims, late return, privacy.

callouts.title: Handover record
callouts.text: Filled in at release and return.

callouts.title: Signatures
callouts.text: Blank lines when printed; drawn signatures when signed online.

callouts.title: Fingerprint
callouts.text: Any change to the terms would change this code.

title: Rental step 8 · Renter: sign electronically
purpose: To sign, the renter ticks “I agree”, types the full name exactly as on the account and draws the signature with a finger or mouse.
example: Carla Mendoza signs before pickup.

callouts.title: Signature pad
callouts.text: Saved as an image on the contract.

callouts.title: Sign
callouts.text: Records the time and the fingerprint signed.

title: Rental step 9 · Owner: sign (or record a paper copy)
purpose: The owner signs the same way. Instead, both can sign the printed contract at pickup; the owner then uploads a photo of the signed page and it counts as signed by both.
example: Carla has signed; Olga signs online.

callouts.title: Paper option
callouts.text: For renters who prefer to sign on paper.

title: Rental step 10 · Contract signed by both
purpose: Both signatures appear on the contract with the time they were made. The vehicle cannot be released before this point.
example: Signed electronically by Olga Navarro and Carla Mendoza.

callouts.title: Fingerprint
callouts.text: Each signature records the code it agreed to.

title: Rental step 11 · Renter: pay the full amount
purpose: The renter pays the rental fee and the deposit before pickup. The first part of any payment fills the deposit; a cashier verifies each payment.
example: Carla pays ₱13,000 by GCash (reference 7055501234567).

title: Rental step 12 · Owner: release with readings and 6 photos
purpose: At pickup the owner checks the renter’s license and ID, walks around the vehicle with the renter, records the odometer, fuel level and condition, and takes 6 photos. Release is refused until full payment is verified and the contract is signed.
example: 52,310 km, fuel 3/4, small scratch on the rear bumper.

callouts.title: Payments verified
callouts.text: Deposit and rental fee in full.

callouts.title: Odometer and fuel
callouts.text: Copied into the contract’s handover record.

callouts.title: 6 required photos
callouts.text: Front, back, both sides, odometer, fuel gauge.

title: Rental step 13 · Renter: check the release record (before)
purpose: The renter sees the 6 photos and the readings and either confirms them or reports what is different. The contract also asks the renter to share location while driving.
example: The vehicle is Active. Carla has not answered yet and is not sharing location.

callouts.title: Report a difference
callouts.text: With a note, sent to the owner.

callouts.title: Share location
callouts.text: Required by the contract while driving.

title: Rental step 14 · Renter: confirmed and sharing location (after)
purpose: The release record is confirmed and the phone shares the location while the renter drives. Only the owner and ZamMove staff can see it, and only until the return.
example: Carla confirmed the record; location sent every 15 seconds.

callouts.title: Sharing
callouts.text: Keep the page open while driving.

title: Rental step 15 · Owner: rental map
purpose: The owner follows each rented-out vehicle on a live map with its recent route, pickup and return points. Leaving Zamboanga City turns the marker red and notifies the owner.
example: ZAM 5150 driven by Carla, heading towards Pasonanca.

callouts.title: Status
callouts.text: Live and when it last updated.

title: Rental step 16 · Owner: record the return
purpose: At return the owner records the odometer, fuel and condition again with 6 new photos. Tracking stops and the route is deleted.
example: 52,480 km (170 km driven), fuel 3/4, a new scratch on the left door.

callouts.title: Readings at return
callouts.text: Cannot be lower than at release.

title: Rental step 17 · Owner: complete, or claim part of the deposit
purpose: After inspecting the vehicle the owner either completes the rental (full deposit refunded) or, within 3 days, claims part of the deposit with photos and the amount.
example: Olga claims ₱4,500 of the ₱8,000 deposit for repainting the left door.

title: Rental step 18 · Renter: accept or dispute the claim
purpose: The renter sees the claim with the owner’s photos and either accepts it or disputes it with a reason. A dispute goes to a ZamMove administrator.
example: Carla disputes: the scratch is in the release photos.

title: Rental step 19 · Administrator: decide the dispute
purpose: The administrator compares the release and return photos with both explanations and decides how much of the deposit is kept (up to the claimed amount).
example: Ada decides ₱1,500 instead of ₱4,500.

title: Rental step 20 · Renter: completed and deposit refunded
purpose: The rental is completed. The settlement shows the deposit, the amount kept for the claim and the refund.
example: ₱8,000 deposit − ₱1,500 kept = ₱6,500 refunded.

title: Rental step 21 · The finished contract
purpose: The contract now holds the whole rental: readings and photos at release and return, the renter’s answers, the deposit settlement and both signatures. Both parties can read or print it any time.
example: Released at 52,310 km, returned at 52,480 km; ₱6,500 refunded.

title: Customer home (returning customer)
purpose: A returning customer’s home: start a booking or rental, follow trips in progress, popular routes.
example: Carla Mendoza has a trip in progress and a completed trip.

callouts.title: Your trips
callouts.text: Active and completed trips, amount paid, Track button.

callouts.title: Popular routes
callouts.text: One tap fills the booking form.

title: Driver profile
purpose: Who accepted the booking: photo, rating, trips, vehicle and recent reviews. Address, birthday and license number are never shown.
example: Ramon Cruz · ★5.0 · silver Mitsubishi L300, plate ZAM 7810.

callouts.title: Photo and rating
callouts.text: Verified badge, stars, trips, driving since.

title: Report an incident
purpose: Report a problem on a trip (delay, damage, missing items, driver conduct). Staff investigate each case.
example: IN-4RT6YB: driver arrived 40 minutes late (Medium), under review.

title: Payment history and receipts
purpose: Every payment, how it was paid and whether it is confirmed. Receipts open from here.
example: BK-7Q2M4X down payment: ₱1,000 GCash + ₱270.50 cash.

title: Notifications
purpose: Updates about bookings, payments and rentals appear under the bell.
example: Items loaded · Payment confirmed · Rental approved.

title: Profile and photo
purpose: Personal details, profile photo, alerts and shortcuts. Drivers’ photos are shown to customers.
example: Dina Reyes with a profile photo.

callouts.title: Profile photo
callouts.text: On the driver card and profile.

title: Driver dashboard
purpose: Availability switch, assigned vehicle, open requests and active trips.
example: Dina Reyes, white L300 ZAM 4521, one active trip.

callouts.title: Workspace switcher
callouts.text: Switch between Customer, Driver and Owner.

callouts.title: Driver menu
callouts.text: Dashboard, Requests, Active trip, My vehicle, Earnings.

title: Driver: my vehicle
purpose: The vehicle the admin assigned to this driver, with its details and status.
example: Mitsubishi L300, ZAM 4521, owned by Olga Navarro.

callouts.title: My vehicle
callouts.text: Plate, type, capacity, owner and status.

title: Apply to be a driver or vehicle owner
purpose: Any customer can apply by uploading documents. Staff verify, interview and orient applicants before approval.
example: Pending review → Under verification → Interview → Orientation → Approved.

callouts.title: Documents
callouts.text: License, ID, clearance, proof of address.

title: Vehicle owner dashboard
purpose: Fleet summary: registered, approved, pending and assigned vehicles.
example: Olga Navarro owns 9 vehicles.

callouts.title: Owner menu
callouts.text: Dashboard, Vehicles, Rentals, Drivers, Trip history.

title: Vehicles
purpose: Every registered vehicle, its approval and operating status. New vehicles need admin approval.
example: Isuzu Forward (ZAM 9902) is waiting for verification.

callouts.title: Vehicle card
callouts.text: Plate, type, color, year, registration, driver.

title: Register a vehicle
purpose: Vehicle details and the OR/CR. Hauling vehicles take bookings with a driver; passenger types are rental-only.
example: Hauling: 3-Wheeler, Pickup, L300, Closed Van, 6-Wheeler. Rental only: Sedan, SUV, Passenger Van.

title: Drivers
purpose: Assign an approved driver to a vehicle or recommend one; an admin approves each assignment.
example: Dina, Ramon and Leo drive Olga’s L300s.

title: Trip history
purpose: Every trip made with the owner’s vehicles.
example: Completed trips by Dina, Ramon and Leo.

title: Remittance queue
purpose: Check each driver’s weekly remittance against GCash or cash received; verify or record a shortfall.
example: Dina Reyes remitted ₱1,739.20.

title: Payments to verify
